definitions.explanation: A person who stubbornly refuses to change their mind, habits, or ways of doing things. Can be used both critically and with a tone of grudging respect.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{頑固者|がんこもの}だ。
examples.english: My father is a stubborn person.

examples.japanese: あの{職人|しょくにん}は{頑固者|がんこもの}で、{自分|じぶん}のやり{方|かた}を{変|か}えない。
examples.english: That craftsman is stubborn and won't change his way of doing things.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{頑固者|がんこもの}だが、{家族|かぞく}のことを{誰|だれ}よりも{大切|たいせつ}に{思|おも}っている。
examples.english: My grandfather is stubborn, but he cares about his family more than anyone.

notes:
A compound of {頑固|がんこ} (stubborn) and {者|もの} (person). Often used to describe older men, particularly fathers and grandfathers, and carries a mix of criticism and affection. In the context of craftsmen and artisans, being a {頑固者|がんこもの} can be positive, implying uncompromising dedication to quality.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {頑固者|がんこもの}の{親父|おやじ}: a stubborn old man (father)
- {筋金入|すじがねい}りの{頑固者|がんこもの}: a thoroughly stubborn person
- {昔|むかし}ながらの{頑固者|がんこもの}: an old-fashioned stubborn person

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {意地|いじ}っ{張|ぱ}り: obstinate person — more colloquial; implies stubbornness driven by pride or spite
- {頑固|がんこ}な{人|ひと}: stubborn person — the adjective form; more neutral than the compound {頑固者|がんこもの}
- {強情|ごうじょう}な{人|ひと}: obstinate person — emphasizes willful refusal to yield
